records.name: NextFab
records.summary: A North Philadelphia makerspace with laser cutters, 3D printers, woodshops, metal and sewing tools, and electronics benches. Free tours and public events let you look around before you join.
records.what_you_do: Take classes, use the tools, and join the member community. Several of its free Repair Fairs are held here.

schedule.text: Open Saturday through Thursday from 10 am to 8 pm. Closed on Fridays. Classes run on their own dates.

cost.text: Membership is needed for classes and shop use: $149 a month, month to month, or $134.10 a month on a yearly agreement. A discounted $129 a month applies to students, educators, military, seniors, first responders and others. Tours are free.

access.notes: The building is described as ADA compliant, with a paved, ramped entrance, a load-in garage, and gender-neutral restrooms near the workshops. Some workshop areas and machines may be hard to use for some physical disabilities, so ask about accommodations. Classes assume you can follow instruction in English on your own. Nearest SEPTA rail, per the FAQ: the Berks stop on the Market-Frankford Line, about five blocks east. Bus Routes 3 and 57 and the Girard Avenue trolley also run nearby.

requirements.gear: You may bring your own hand tools. Power tools and unusual items need instructor permission first.

first_step.how: Book a free tour through the website, then ask about membership before you plan a class or a project on the machines.
first_step.basis: Free tours and public events let you see the space before you pay, but classes and shop use need a paid membership and a proficiency check.
first_step.what_to_expect: A free tour walks you through the North Philadelphia space, including the jewelry, sewing, woodworking, metal, and laser cutting areas. Before you use the machines, you finish an online orientation and then pass a proficiency check, a private lesson, or a class. Ask when you book how long a tour runs.
first_visit_tips: Book the tour through the website before you come.
Free on-site parking is open to visitors as well as members.
Check the events page for free public gatherings that non-members can join.
Ask an instructor before you bring any power tools or unusual items.

records.notes: Membership prices come from the FAQ. The FAQ says members must be 18 or older for shop use, yet it also lists junior memberships for ages 10 to 17 with an adult, so kids_ok is left out until NextFab confirms. The classes page lists no class prices, no beginner classes, and no dated classes. Tour booking steps and length are not on the pages read. The Repair Fairs line is carried over from tier 1; none appear on the October 2026 events list.

records.name: Northeast Philly Toastmasters Club (Club 1134526)
records.summary: A Northeast Philadelphia Toastmasters club that practices public speaking and meets online on Zoom. Guests attend free after an RSVP and choose for themselves whether to speak.
records.what_you_do: Join an online meeting to try speaking, answer impromptu questions, or just watch and say what brought you.

schedule.text: Online on Zoom every other Tuesday evening, 7 to 9 pm, usually the 1st and 3rd Tuesdays.

first_step.how: RSVP for a guest seat on the club's Meetup page. The Zoom link is posted there after you RSVP.
first_step.basis: The club says guests are welcome at any skill level, speaking is optional for guests, and its pages explain how to RSVP.
first_step.what_to_expect: A guest joins the Zoom meeting and watches members give prepared speeches, speak off the cuff, and run the meeting roles, followed by feedback. You are asked what brought you to the meeting and, at the close, what you thought of it. Speaking is your choice, and the visit costs nothing.
first_visit_tips: RSVP on the club's Meetup page first, since the Zoom link appears only after you do.
Decide before the meeting whether you want to take part in the impromptu speaking, since guests choose.
Check the Meetup page for cancellations, because the club posts changes there.
Meeting times are shown in your own local time on the club's site.

records.notes: The club's pages disagree on the schedule. The directions page describes Zoom meetings every other Tuesday; the meetings page says no upcoming meetings are published yet; and the contact page says the next meeting is a date to be announced. Confirm the next meeting on Meetup before a visit. The club plans to return to an in-person room at Jefferson Health Torresdale, 10800 Knights Road, Philadelphia, but gives no date. The contact page lists an automated club address and asks visitors not to write to it, so the Gmail address and phone from the directions page are kept and the Meetup RSVP is the first step. Tier 1 had Tuesdays at 7 pm from a national listing; the club's own directions page now gives 7 to 9 pm.

records.name: Ocean Blue Project Philadelphia River Cleanups
records.summary: A national group that runs trash cleanups on Philadelphia's rivers and creeks, including the Delaware waterfront, the Schuylkill River Trail, Penn's Landing, and Fairmount Park riverbanks.
records.what_you_do: Pick up litter along the riverbanks during cleanups that usually last 1 to 2 hours, held rain or shine.

schedule.text: Cleanups are posted by date as they are scheduled. They usually last 1 to 2 hours and go ahead rain or shine.

locations.label: Delaware River waterfront, Schuylkill River Trail, Penn's Landing, Fairmount Park riverbanks

cost.text: No participation fee is stated on the group's pages. Gloves, bags, and tools are provided.

requirements.gear: Supplies are provided. Bring comfortable outdoor clothes, closed-toe shoes, and a reusable water bottle, plus sun protection or rain gear as needed.

first_step.how: Watch the Philadelphia River Cleanup listing on the group's site for a date, then join that cleanup. You can also email the office to ask about upcoming Philadelphia dates.
first_step.basis: The group says no experience is needed and cleanups suit all levels, and it offers a way to join, but no Philadelphia date is posted right now.
first_step.what_to_expect: A cleanup lasts about 1 to 2 hours along a riverbank, and you pick up litter with a group. Supplies are handed out at the start, with a kickoff briefing. Every volunteer signs a release and waiver that is brought to the site on the day, and a minor needs a parent or guardian to sign.
first_visit_tips: Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable outdoor clothes, and bring a reusable water bottle.
Fill in the release and waiver before the day and bring it with you.
Bring sun protection or rain gear, since cleanups go ahead rain or shine.
Ask the office for the meeting spot if the listing does not show one.

records.notes: No Philadelphia cleanup has a date on the group's pages as of 2026-10-08, and the national events page lists no Philadelphia entries. The volunteer page also describes a DIY route: register a cleanup and receive a cleanup guide by email. The release has an under-18 box with a parent or guardian signature, but no minimum age is given. The rain or shine line and supply list come from the Philadelphia cleanup page.

records.name: OIC Philadelphia Financial Literacy Classes
records.summary: A job training nonprofit that teaches budgeting, banking, credit and saving alongside its job and adult education classes. One-on-one money coaching is also offered.
records.what_you_do: Build a working budget, set up a simple savings plan, check your credit report, and make a personal money plan.

locations.label: OIC Philadelphia, N Broad and Thompson streets

cost.text: Free workshops and coaching for Philadelphia residents, per OIC's financial empowerment page. Confirm before you enroll.

first_step.how: Call (215) 236-7700 and ask for the next money skills workshop or coaching session by name. The site does not list class dates.
first_step.basis: Open to Philadelphia residents, with a phone line and inquiry form, but class dates and format are not published.
first_step.what_to_expect: Workshops cover budgets, saving, credit reports, opening a bank account, and debt, and coaching is one-on-one. Both are free for Philadelphia residents. Ask on the phone how long a workshop runs and whether it meets in person or online, since the site does not say.
first_visit_tips: Have a valid state ID handy, since the job training programs ask for one.
If you are also looking at job training, it asks for a high school diploma or GED and a passing entrance assessment.
Ask for the financial workshop by name, because the inquiry form is built for job training programs.

records.notes: Audience is set to residents because the financial empowerment page says Philadelphia residents can access the free workshops; tier 1 had public. The job training track on the inquiry page asks for a high school diploma or GED, a passing entrance assessment, a valid state ID, and an interview. Those rules are for job training, not the money workshops. Newest dates: April 1, 2026 (blog post on the financial literacy page) and August 19, 2025 (blog on the financial empowerment page). The page has no current class schedule. The city's Financial Empowerment Centers offer free counseling, but they are a city service, so they are not listed as a lead.

records.name: Old Academy Players
records.summary: A community theater on Indian Queen Lane where every role is filled by an unpaid volunteer, and where crew help is needed for set and tech strike and build sessions.
records.what_you_do: Audition for a play, or ask the director how to help with sets, tech, or hospitality for a show.

schedule.text: Audition and crew times are posted for each show on the auditions page.

cost.text: Roles are unpaid volunteer roles. Membership is optional: dues are $25 for a first year, $38 a year after that, or $60 for a couple, paid annually.

access.notes: The nearest SEPTA stop is the East Falls Regional Rail station on the Manayunk/Norristown Line, a short walk away, per the theater's directions page. Queen Lane station is about a mile away.

first_step.how: Come to a posted public audition (the next listed is Venus in Fur on Saturday, November 7, 2026 at 10 am), or fill in the contact form and choose the option for volunteering and membership information.
first_step.basis: Auditions are open to the public with set dates and a clear sign-in, but the page does not say beginners are welcome, and crew sign-up goes through the director.
first_step.what_to_expect: An audition is a sign-in at the theater on a Saturday morning. Bring a short dramatic monologue, a headshot, and a theatrical resume, and expect that some people are asked to read a scene cold. Every role is unpaid, and you do not need to be a member to take part.
first_visit_tips: For Venus in Fur, fill in the audition form ahead of time and sign in before 11:30 am.
For Bug, check in in person by 12:30 pm, first come, first served. Video auditions are not accepted for either show.
Parking is free in the private lot behind the theater.
Read the role descriptions on the auditions page before you prepare, since many roles list an age range or a gender.

records.notes: Membership page: dues are $25 for a first year, $38 a year after that, and $60 for married or long-term partnered couples. Members get free Club Night, voting rights at General Meetings, and a newsletter. The Bug notice says past performers must be members or renew, so membership matters for returning performers. The dues payment page had only a title, so nothing was taken from it. The theater address is 3544 on the audition page and 3540 to 3544 on the contact page; this record uses 3544. The contact page lists no email, so the director email carried over from tier 1 is unverified; the phone and the volunteering contact form are the published routes. Crew sign-up has no published process, and the audition page sends questions to the director.

records.name: Olney Culture Lab
records.summary: Runs festivals, events, podcasts and partnerships that celebrate the many cultures of the Olney neighborhood in North Philadelphia. It has operated since 2014.
records.what_you_do: Go to a neighborhood festival, check the events calendar, or sign up for email updates.

schedule.text: Festivals and events through the year, listed on the events calendar.

cost.text: Check each event listing for cost. The calendar marks some events as free.

first_step.how: Check the events calendar for the next event and go, or sign up for updates with the Get Updates form in the site footer.
first_step.basis: Events are public, the calendar shows each one, and the site offers an email update sign-up.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events celebrate the neighborhood's many cultures with youth arts, a community dinner, and performances by local artists. Each calendar listing shows the venue, the time, and whether the event is free.
first_visit_tips: Check the calendar listing for the venue and time before you go, since events move between places.
The group's office is in Center City, so go by the event listing rather than the office address.
Join the Get Updates list in the footer so new events reach you.

records.notes: The events calendar lists one event: the Olney Youth Arts Festival and A Taste of Olney Community Dinner, on November 7, 2026, 12:30 to 7 pm, at Thurgood Marshall Elementary School, 5120 North 6th Street, marked free. The homepage has a news item dated October 7, 2026 about the same festival, which is why the last sign of life is 2026-10. Tier 1 recorded the festival date as October 7; the calendar date is November 7, so the schedule text no longer mentions a festival date. The signature events page names the festival as November 8, 2025 and mixes older programs, so it was not used for dates. The contact page's office address, 1315 Walnut St., Suite 300, Philadelphia, PA 19107, is an office, not an event venue. Volunteer roles are not described on the pages read.

records.name: Operation Save Our City
records.summary: Runs Sunshine House in Kensington, a support space for people dealing with addiction. It also does outreach, community clean-ups, food drives and overdose-reversal (Narcan) training.
records.what_you_do: Sign up through the Volunteer button on the Sunshine House page, or contact the group to ask what help is needed right now.

cost.text: No fees are listed. Donations go through the group's fundraising page.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer sign-up form from the Volunteer button on the Sunshine House page, then call (267) 804-7166 or email to ask about hours and a first shift.
first_step.basis: A volunteer sign-up form is posted and training workshops are offered, but the site does not describe what a volunteer shift involves.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunshine House on Kensington Avenue is a safe indoor place to rest, with a messaging center where you can call or leave messages for family, clothing and hygiene supplies, snacks, and wound-care supplies. Overdose-reversal training and volunteer education workshops are offered. Volunteers help run these services, so the sign-up form is the way in.
first_visit_tips: Confirm hours by phone or email before you come, since the website does not list them.
Ask about the overdose-reversal (Narcan) training when you sign up; the Sunshine House page links to a training sign-up.
Ask the group about the best way to get there, since the site gives no transit directions.

records.notes: One WebSearch found no confirmed Sunshine House hours. A community food directory lists weekday meal times, but it is undated and covers food only, so it was not recorded. The address, phone, and email come from the group's contact page. Volunteer roles and training requirements are not described, and the contact page gives no background check information. The Inquirer article dated January 14, 2025 is the newest dated item found.

leads_only.note: Named on Olney Culture Lab's homepage as the organization it is a project of. Link not found; url is the page where it was named. Not checked.

leads_only.note: Named on Olney Culture Lab's signature events page as co-running the monthly Second Friday Open Mic at St. Paul's Lutheran Church. Not checked.

notes: Seven groups. 30 fetches and 1 WebSearch used. No pages blocked. The Old Academy dues payment page returned only a title, so it was not used. Olney's festival date conflicts with tier 1 and Toastmasters' schedule pages disagree; both are explained in those records. Sunshine House hours were not found on the group's site or in the one search. One mistake: a Docs read tool was called by accident; it was refused with no effect. Budget not exhausted.
